newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Hebron Jews arrested after seizing casbah houses.
newsitem.headline: Hebron Jews arrested after seizing casbah houses.

text.p: Israeli security forces chased Jewish settlers across Hebron rooftops on Wednesday to break up a protest against an imminent deal to hand over most of the West Bank town to Palestinians.

Witnesses said police arrested about 20 Jews after disturbances that began with the settlers' illegal pre-dawn takeover of two vacant houses in Hebron's Arab casbah. Soldiers and police evacuated the settlers from the houses.
Disturbances spread to the rooftops and the streets where settlers scuffled with soldiers, hurling eggs, apples and stones, witnesses said. Israel Radio said a boy was injured.
Hebron's Jews are angry that a U.S.-brokered Israeli-PLO summit made progress on Tuesday towards Israel's long-overdue handover of 80 percent of the flashpoint town.

The 400 settlers in the heart of the town of 100,000 Arabs fear Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu will endanger their security if he signs the deal expected soon with Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat.
"We are not speaking of toppling the government. We are speaking of toppling the deal," settler woman Orit Struck told Israeli army radio.
The town, captured by Israel with the rest of the West Bank in the 1967 Middle East war, is the last Palestinian town due to be given self-rule.
"What's going on?" Palestinians asked when the disturbances began. "I'm afraid. I expect there will be a massacre," said Bassam Ahmaro, a 35-year-old Palestinian.

A Jewish settler from the neighbouring Kiryat Arba enclave killed 29 Palestinians kneeling in prayer nearly three years ago in the sacred town's al-Ibrahimi mosque, known to Jews as the tomb of the biblical patriarch Abraham.

Hebron's settlers feel betrayed by Netanyahu, a rightist backer of Jewish settlement in occupied lands who has nonetheless promised to uphold the 1995 self-rule deal on Hebron signed by the left-leaning government he ousted in May.
"We'll not allow a violation of the law," Netanyahu's Public Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani told Israel Radio. "We must uphold the law everywhere on both sides."

Some members of Netanyahu's government coalition have come out against the Hebron deal, which officials say could be signed within a week. Deputy Education Minister Moshe Peled was among those to turn out in a show of solidarity with the settlers.
Jews of Hebron say they would expand their community but the Israeli government prevents them from buying property and limits them to building only in existing Jewish neighbourhoods.
The settlers said one house they took over was Jewish property and the other a building -- abutting a Jewish enclave -- they fear the PLO will use to house guerrillas.

"Netanyahu will leave Hebron and the terrorists will be 20 meters (yards) away from you police and soldiers," a settler shouted over a loudspeaker at the security forces. "We are protecting you by our protests."
The Arab casbah is in the 20 percent of Hebron due to remain under Israeli occupation in the deal along with Jewish enclaves.
The fate of the Jews in Hebron and in other West Bank settlements will be decided in "final-status" talks between Israel and the Palestinians due to be completed by May 1999.
